headline: The leveling core is unusually well specified and directly implementable: each level-up gives +1 to EVERY stat automatically PLUS 5 freely allocable points (webtoon ch. 14), with a further +3 for completing a daily fitness quest. The five stats are Strength (attack power/speed), Agility (reaction/evasion; crit rate+damage in the game adaptation), Stamina/Vitality (max HP + regen), Intelligence (max MP + MP regen; cooldown reduction in-game), and Sense/Perception (danger sense; in-game it raises MINIMUM damage — a damage-floor stat, not a crit stat). Class advancement is one scripted event at level 40: a solo survival dungeon where accumulated survival time buys the tier of class you are offered. On gates: E/D/C/B/A/S is set by measured mana quantity+quality, gate size scales with rank (D ≈ a large door, S ≈ "like a hurricane"), uncleared gates break after 7 days, and the most implementable rule found is the boss-rank offset — the wiki monster table shows trash at gate rank ±1 while the true boss sits a full rank ABOVE the gate. On environments the brief's claim is directionally right but the break point is wrong: E and D are caves/subway interiors as claimed, but C-rank in canon is still cave systems (both the C-rank insect and goblin dungeons are cave tunnels), and even an A-rank gate is described as a "basic cave." The real discontinuity is at B, because red gates only occur at B+ and are explicitly not normal dungeons — scorching desert, poisonous jungle, frostbite snowfield — with S-rank/instant/field dungeons supplying the full landscapes (burning ruined city as a 100-floor tower, walled desert pyramid complex, glacier world carrying a -30% attack speed / -30% move speed debuff, ant-infested island). Shadow raising costs ZERO mana to cast, has a failure rate explicitly "proportional to the target's stats and the time elapsed since death," allows exactly 3 attempts per corpse, and starts at a hard cap of 20 shadows that grows with the mana pool (i.e. Intelligence) — with 7 shadow grades from Normal to a single Grand Marshal, promotion gated on explicit owner authorization, and shadow strength scaling off the OWNER's authority, Intelligence and level rather than being fixed per shadow. Combat feel rests on a reactive perfect-dodge with i-frames plus slow-motion and a free counter, a three-tier break/stagger gauge, positional back-attack bonuses, and conditional finishers that fire when the enemy is knocked down, airborne, or freshly dodged.
risks: LEGAL: the biggest exposure is not mechanics but naming and silhouette. Mechanics, stat formulas, rank ladders and progression curves are not copyrightable, but a red-and-black knight with a greatsword guarding an empty throne, a giant humanoid ant lieutenant, or a 100-floor tower explicitly presented as a burning real-world capital city would read as copies of specific character/scene designs. Keep the MECHANIC (checkpoint-boss tower, named lieutenant shadow, ruined-city biome) and discard the specific silhouette, palette and setting.

The E/D/C/B/A/S letter ladder plus the terms 'gate', 'dungeon break', 'hunter', 'guild', 'mana crystal', 'awakening' are genre-common across dozens of Korean litRPG works and are safe. But 'Shadow Monarch', 'Monarch' as the proper noun for the top-tier antagonist class, 'Red Gate' as a capitalised proper noun, and 'Ruler' are strongly associated with the source. The repo already ships 'MONARCH'S REACH' and 'THE RIFT MONARCH' in src/game/config.js — 'monarch' as a common noun for a boss is defensible, but it is the single closest term to the source in the codebase and is worth renaming to something like 'Sovereign', 'Archon' or 'Crownbearer' for cheap distance.

Almost every hard number below comes from fan wikis, not a primary rulebook. The '5 stat points per level' figure is well attested (fandom cites webtoon ch. 14, and the licensed game independently uses 5/level), but there is NO canonical XP table, no canonical mana cost list, and no canonical per-point conversion rate. Any 'X points = Y% damage' number must be invented for the game, not sourced.

Sources contradict each other on red-gate time dilation. Fandom and Beebom both state 1 hour outside = 1 day inside; one search summary asserted the inverse (days inside = hours outside, which is the same claim stated backwards) and another framed the 7-day break timer as an escape route. Treat 1h outside : 24h inside as the intended ratio and be aware fan summaries garble it.

Hunter-population numbers in the source are internally inconsistent: the wiki says ~0.001% of the global population awakens and only 0.0002% reach C or above, yet also says ~50,000 awakened exist in South Korea out of ~51 million people (0.098%, roughly 100x higher). Do not build economy or rarity math on either figure without picking one and owning it.

The canonical progression is a power fantasy with almost no failure states after the midpoint, and reviewers of the licensed action game specifically criticise it for devolving into 'mashing buttons while cycling through cooldowns' with moves that 'don't really flow together well or cancel properly'. Faithfully reproducing the source curve will produce a game that stops being interesting around the B-rank gate unless the break gauge, dodge windows and cancel rules carry the tension that raw numbers no longer do.

The shadow army is the fantasy's payload but is also an aggro/perf hazard on Android. Canon scales to 100,000+ then 10,000,000+ entities. The licensed mobile game solved this by deploying only 3 shadow LEADERS at a time, each spawning a small retinue, on-field for 15-20 seconds then despawning. The repo currently allows maxShadows: 3 persistent — a timed-summon model is both closer to the shippable precedent and cheaper on a phone.

Carry-capacity growth in canon is not a smooth curve — it is 20, then a story-gated jump to 100,000+, then 10,000,000+. A literal implementation produces a dead progression axis for most of the game. Capacity must be re-authored as a smooth function of the Intelligence stat if it is to be a meaningful build decision.

The repo's current config.js diverges from the genre on three points that fans WILL notice: POINTS_PER_LEVEL is 3 rather than 5, there is no Sense/Perception stat (only str/agi/vit/int), and there is no automatic +1-to-all-stats on level-up. The auto +1 is the cheapest fix and is what makes early levels feel like the body itself is changing rather than just a number.

Gate biomes in the repo are currently 1:1 with rank (E=hollow, D=catacomb, C=glacier, B=ember, A=void, S=monarch). That is a defensible design but it is NOT how the source works — the source ties interior class to gate TYPE with rank only weighting the roll, which is what produces the 'we scanned it as C-rank and walked into a snowfield' moment. Hard-coupling biome to rank forfeits the genre's best surprise beat.

headline: Gatebreaker is a ~7,700-line Three.js ARPG whose *shipping* game is only ~5,100 lines: `main.js` → `Game` (game.js) → `World` (game/world.js), with screens as plain DOM divs toggled by `UI`. The single most important finding for an extension team is that **2,600 lines (34% of src) are already written but completely unreferenced dead code**: `src/world/overworld.js` (353) + `src/world/terrain.js` (155) are a finished seeded-heightfield open world with per-rank portal placement, and `src/game/attacks.js` (1220) + `src/game/weapons.js` (872) are a finished sweep-hitbox/poise/boss-phase combat system and an 8-weapon loot system with rarity and affixes. None of them are imported by anything — `attacks.js`/`weapons.js` duplicate functionality that `game.js` implements inline and worse, and `overworld.js` is exactly the "city hub with portal entrances" feature, already built and orphaned. `physics.js` was explicitly designed for both level types (`setEnvironment(FLAT_GROUND | terrainHeight, resolve)`) and is the one piece genuinely ready. The hard blockers are: there is no screen state machine (`Game.state` is a 4-string flag and `update()` hardcodes the dungeon update path); enemies and shadows do not use `CharacterBody` at all, so they cannot traverse terrain or step over anything; "biomes" are 5 hex colors applied to identical hardcoded arena geometry; and the shipped HDRI silently overrides all per-biome image-based lighting, so all six biomes currently light identically.
risks: DEAD CODE IS THE HEADLINE RISK: src/world/overworld.js, src/world/terrain.js, src/game/attacks.js and src/game/weapons.js (2,600 lines, 34% of src) are imported by NOTHING. Verified by grepping every import edge in src/ and confirming no dynamic import() exists. A team told 'the codebase has an overworld' will assume it runs. It has never executed in the browser — the only thing that ever imported it is /Users/jackenholland/gatebreaker/ow-test.mjs, which imports the absolute path '/home/user/collins-seo-website/game/src/world/overworld.js' from a different machine. Treat all four files as unverified drafts, not working code.

NO SCREEN STATE MACHINE EXISTS. Game.state (game.js:70) is a 4-value string 'idle|playing|paused|over' and Game.update() (game.js:689-718) hardcodes `if (this.state === 'playing')` then calls seven dungeon-specific updaters. Screens are DOM divs in index.html toggled by UI.show()/hide() (ui.js:65-66) with transitions wired as hardcoded callback chains through main.js:15-32. There is no router, no per-state update dispatch, and no concept of 'which world am I in'. Adding a city hub is not 'add a screen' — it requires inverting Game.update into a state-dispatch table first.

ENEMIES AND SHADOWS DO NOT USE THE PHYSICS ENGINE. Only the player gets a CharacterBody (game.js:145-146). Enemies integrate manually with `e.vel.addScaledVector(...); e.pos.addScaledVector(e.vel, dt); this.world.resolve(...)` (game.js:874-880) and shadows identically at game.js:1050-1052. Both are hard-pinned to y=0 with no gravity, no ground sampling, no step height. On any terrain or city with elevation they will float, clip through stairs, and walk through raised geometry. This is the single largest hidden cost in the city-hub and biome work.

THE HDRI DEFEATS PER-BIOME LIGHTING TODAY. buildBiomeEnvironment (render/env.js:109-116) returns `gen.fromEquirectangular(_hdriTexture)` and ignores the `biome` argument entirely whenever public/hdri/rift_sky.hdr loaded — which it does, 409KB, loaded at boot in main.js:81. The per-biome synthesized env map (makeEnvSource, env.js:24-67) is only the failure fallback. All six biomes therefore share one identical IBL right now, and the file comment states this is intentional. Any 'distinct biome lighting' work must first decide to fork this function per biome, which re-introduces the PMREM cost the HDRI was added to avoid.

'BIOMES' ARE COLOR SWATCHES, NOT ENVIRONMENTS. config.js:45-52 gives each biome exactly five hex values (fog, ground, accent, sky, pillar). World.build (world.js:52-206) then constructs the SAME hardcoded geometry for every one: CircleGeometry ground, CylinderGeometry membrane wall, TorusGeometry rim, cone pillars, dodecahedron rocks, octahedron shards, one HemisphereLight + one DirectionalLight + one rim light + one PointLight. Fog is always `new THREE.Fog(biome.fog, radius*0.7, radius*2.6)` (world.js:61). makeSky(biome, {stars, aurora}) (sky.js:79) accepts star/aurora tuning but World.build never passes it, so every sky is stars=1.0, aurora=0.55. Delivering visually distinct biomes is a rewrite of World.build, not a config edit.

SHADOW ARMY CAP IS HARDCODED IN THREE PLACES AND SHADOWS HAVE NO IDENTITY. The live cap is `const MAX_BOUND = 6` (game.js:15), the per-cast raise limit is SKILLS.summon.maxShadows=3 (config.js:89), and retention re-hardcodes the literal at `this.save.shadows = Math.min(6, this.shadows.length)` (game.js:1189). Worse, save.shadows is an INTEGER COUNT (save.js:12), not a roster — shadows have no name, level, type or equipment, and are rebuilt from scratch each run at game.js:200. A real shadow army needs a save-schema change from a number to an array, which the merge-on-load in save.js:18-34 will tolerate but every read site must be updated.

NO PATHFINDING ANYWHERE. Enemy AI is a three-branch string switch on e.base.ai ('chase'|'lunge'|'ranged') inline in _updateEnemies (game.js:831-871): steer straight at the player, push out of obstacles via World.resolve, then O(n^2) crowd separation (_separate, game.js:996-1011). This works only because the arena is a flat disc with convex cylinder obstacles. Any concave geometry — a building, a wall, an alley — traps enemies permanently. A walkable city requires a navmesh or flow field that does not exist in any form.

CIRCULAR-ARENA ASSUMPTIONS ARE BAKED INTO NON-WORLD CODE. Projectile culling tests `Math.hypot(pr.pos.x, pr.pos.z) > this.world.radius + 2` (game.js:1070); boss spawn position is `new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, -this.world.radius * 0.55)` (game.js:283); World.resolve's final clamp is a radial `lim = this.radius - radius - 0.6` (world.js:309-316); World.randomSpawn is polar-only (world.js:319-328). Every one of these breaks in a non-circular hub and none of them live in the World class where you would look for them.

CAMERA IS A FIXED OFFSET WITH NO COLLISION. camOffset is a constant `new THREE.Vector3(0, 11, 11)` (game.js:50) and _updateCamera (game.js:1162-1177) only lerps position and look-at. In a city with buildings the camera will pass straight through walls. There is also no camera yaw control at all — the player cannot rotate the view, which is acceptable in a disc arena and unacceptable in an explorable hub.

EVERY TEST TOOL IS NON-RUNNABLE ON THIS MACHINE. All 8 Playwright tools in tools/ hardcode the Linux path executablePath:'/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome', and screenshot tools hardcode OUT='/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-collins-seo-website/...'. Each also hardcodes a DIFFERENT dev-server port with no coordination: smoke.mjs 4193, playtest.mjs 4180, progression-test.mjs 4191, pillartest.mjs 4178, land.mjs 4190, hdri-check.mjs 4200, jump-test.mjs / jumpcut-test.mjs / physics-defects-test.mjs 4212 — while vite.config.js:21 serves on 5173. Nothing in package.json runs them (scripts are only dev/build/preview/sync/apk). The verification suite must be repaired before it can gate any of this work.

GAME OWNS ONE WORLD INSTANCE, CONSTRUCTED EAGERLY. `this.world = new World(this.scene, this.renderer, this.camera)` (game.js:54) and World.build() destroys and rebuilds in place (world.js:52). _applyQuality reaches into `this.world.key` (game.js:101-112) to retune the directional light by name. Supporting a second world type means either making World an interface both implementations satisfy (Overworld.resolve already matches World.resolve's signature, which helps) or teaching Game to hold two. The one thing that already works in your favour is that `this._arenaResolve` (game.js:144) closes over `this.world` rather than capturing it, so swapping this.world redirects player collision for free.

SAVE HAS NO SCHEMA VERSIONING BEYOND THE KEY STRING. save.js:3 pins 'gatebreaker.save.v1' and load() merges parsed data onto freshSave() (save.js:23-30), which safely ADDS new fields but has no migration path for CHANGED field types — exactly what converting save.shadows from number to array requires. There is no version integer inside the payload to branch on.

headline: The pack is 106 unique models shipped in 3 formats (OBJ+MTL, FBX, .blend) plus 107 1000x1000 icon PNGs, 97 MB on disk, CC0/Quaternius, and it is 100% handheld items and props — 12 melee weapons, 6 ranged, 18 armor/jewelry, 22 potions, 7 containers, 10 books/scrolls, 6 treasure, 9 crystals, 4 keys, 7 UI symbols, 4 bone props, 1 food. Zero characters, zero creatures, zero buildings, zero terrain, zero vegetation, zero rigs, zero animations, and zero texture files (34 flat-color materials only). So it solves the loot/inventory/weapon-model problem completely and contributes nothing to the world — the city and all 6 biomes still need to be procedural or sourced elsewhere. I confirmed the game has no model loading whatsoever (grep for GLTFLoader/FBXLoader/OBJLoader across src/, public/, index.html returns nothing; all geometry is THREE primitives in src/world/overworld.js, src/game/world.js, src/game/entities.js, src/game/weapons.js). Blender 5.1.2 IS installed (at /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender — note it is NOT on PATH), and I built and verified the entire conversion end to end: all 106 FBX imported into one Blender scene with a deduplicated 34-material palette, exported as a single GLB, then meshopt-compressed. Result: one 758 KB file (406 KB deflated inside the APK) holding all 106 models as exactly-named scene roots, 90,861 triangles total, 27 materials — verified to load through three.js GLTFLoader with the node names intact. Adding the icon atlas (107 icons downscaled to 128px and packed into one 1408x1280 WebP, 319 KB, down from 31 MB) the entire pack costs roughly 755 KB of APK. That is a rounding error against a sane 45-65 MB budget, so the correct strategy is one merged GLB, preloaded whole during the existing 900 ms splash, with per-biome streaming deferred until the environment kits arrive.
risks: The pack supplies nothing for the world. It is 100% handheld props — no characters, creatures, buildings, terrain, or vegetation. If the plan assumes this pack meaningfully advances an open-world city plus 6 biomes, that assumption is wrong: it advances loot and inventory only, and every environmental asset still has to be sourced or stay procedural.

Icon filenames disagree with model filenames by case only (Axe_Small vs Axe_small, FishBone vs Fishbone, Sword_Big vs Sword_big). macOS APFS is case-insensitive so naive lookup works perfectly during development and then fails on Android and in Linux CI. This is a silent ship-breaker unless keys are normalised to lowercase. Potion1_Filled additionally has two icons (Blue/Red) and no exact-name match, needing an explicit alias.

Blender name collision corrupts every node name unless worked around. Creating a handle Empty with the same name as the imported FBX root yields 'Sword001' instead of 'Sword', and every getObjectByName call returns null. I hit this on the first run; the fix (rename imported objects to '<name>__part' first) is in the script but is non-obvious and easy to lose in a rewrite.

Choosing Draco over meshopt introduces a genuine offline-failure mode. DRACOLoader.setDecoderPath() resolves at runtime, and under Capacitor (served from https://localhost with base:'./') a wrong path fails silently, on-device, after packaging — exactly where it is most expensive to find. Draco is only ~20 KB smaller in the APK; that is not worth the risk against the hard no-network requirement.

The source pack is gitignored (.gitignore line 8), so CI cannot regenerate the GLB. If public/models/items.glb is not committed, or is caught by an ignore rule, the build produces a game with no models and no error. The 97 MB source also exists only on this one Mac.

Blender is not on PATH — only at /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender. Any build script that assumes `blender` works will fail with a misleading 'command not found', and will fail differently on a machine where someone has installed Blender via Homebrew.

The 6 named bosses are a real unfilled gap. No free CC0 pack contains anything resembling a Hollow Warden, Frostcaller, Voidweaver, or Rift Monarch. Expect to rescale the closest silhouettes from Ultimate Monsters and carry the identity with colour and the existing glow system — the visual payoff will be weaker than the rest of the upgrade.

Biome-specific set pieces (ice formations, lava, void geometry) are the thinnest area across all free sources. Quaternius and Kenney are strong on generic medieval/fantasy/nature and have essentially nothing for glacier, ember, or void themes. Plan for recolouring a shared modular kit plus procedural shader work rather than expecting to download these.

Art-style collision risk. Poly Haven models are photoscanned PBR realism and will clash badly with flat-shaded low-poly — use Poly Haven for HDRIs and textures only. Mixing Kenney (blocky, colormap atlas) with Quaternius (flat-material, more detailed) in the same scene also reads as inconsistent; pick Quaternius as primary since the pack already in hand is Quaternius.

game-icons.net is CC-BY 3.0, not CC0. Attribution is a licence condition requiring a visible in-game credits screen. Mixamo is likewise not CC0 and forbids redistributing animation files as a library. Both are easy to use casually and then be non-compliant; Quaternius packs ship pre-animated, which avoids Mixamo entirely.

Weapon models are ~2.5x oversized for the game's metre-scale world (Sword is 2.30 units on a ~1.8-unit humanoid). Dropping them in unscaled will look broken and may also break attack-reach tuning if collision volumes are derived from mesh bounds.

Instancing discipline is the real runtime risk, not file size. The current code correctly instances 2,600 grass and 420 rocks. Once city and vegetation kits land, cloning props instead of instancing them will blow past the ~120 draw-call budget on a mid-range phone long before any memory or APK limit is approached.

gltfpack silently strips node names without -kn, and gltf-transform merge produces 106 separate scenes rather than one scene with 106 nodes (three.js would only ever show the first). Both failures are silent and produce a file that loads without error but is unusable.

headline: Target a locked 30 fps for the open city hub and 60 fps for combat arenas on a mid-range 2022-24 Android (Adreno 619 / Mali-G57 class), with a hard ceiling of ~300 draw calls per frame across ALL passes and ~120 in the main opaque pass — WebGL in a Capacitor WebView realistically gets a third of ARM's native "fewer than 500 draw calls per frame" GLES guidance because every call pays JS validation plus driver overhead. Three bugs already in the tree dominate every other consideration and must be fixed before any city work begins: (1) the frame-pacing gate in src/main.js aliases against 72/90/144 Hz panels so those devices run at 36/45/48 fps AND get permanently ratcheted to the 'low' quality tier by src/core/quality.js (fps<46 downgrade threshold) — meaning any profiling done so far on a 90 Hz phone is invalid; (2) src/world/overworld.js:293 toggles PointLight.visible, which changes NUM_POINT_LIGHTS, which is part of three's program cache key (WebGLPrograms.js:450-452), forcing shader recompiles as the player walks; (3) Game.clearEntities (src/game/game.js:209) removes meshes without disposing, and makeHumanoid allocates ~12 fresh geometries + ~6 fresh materials per enemy, leaking roughly 600 geometries per S-rank run — which becomes a hard kill under Android 17's new per-app memory limiter, not just a slowdown. For the city itself: a 64 m grid of chunks gated by Group.visible (three's projectObject early-returns on visible===false, WebGLRenderer.js:1321, pruning the whole subtree from traversal, shadow collection and the second glow-pass traversal), merged BufferGeometry within a chunk, InstancedMesh/BatchedMesh kits across chunks, a fixed 1-hemisphere + 1-directional + PMREM-env light rig with ZERO point lights in every biome (mood comes from a data table of colours/intensities/fog/exposure, not from extra lights), and emissive glow-layer geometry instead of local lights. The current humanoid rig at ~15 draw calls per character is the single biggest structural obstacle to crowds and needs to collapse to ≤6 meshes, then eventually to one vertex-shader-animated InstancedMesh.
risks: The 72/90/144 Hz frame-pacing bug in src/main.js means ANY on-device profiling done so far is invalid, and the quality governor has been pinning those devices to the 'low' tier. Re-baseline on real hardware before trusting a single performance number in this plan or in the repo's history.

30 fps in the city versus 60 fps in combat is a real feel discontinuity. An action game with dodge i-frames (SKILLS.dash has iframes: 0.34) feels materially worse at 30 fps. If the hub has any combat at all, the 30 fps decision needs a design review, not just an engineering one.

The humanoid rig is fundamentally draw-call-hostile. Getting to real crowds (30+) means a vertex-shader animation rewrite of src/game/entities.js plus every animateRig call site in src/game/game.js. That is a multi-day rewrite, not a tweak, and it will fight the existing per-limb Group hierarchy that attacks.js and weapons.js also reach into.

BatchedMesh depends on WEBGL_multi_draw. Where the extension is missing three falls back to a loop of draw calls, so the entire draw-call win evaporates precisely on the weakest devices you most need it on. Feature-detect and keep a merged-geometry fallback path, or the budget silently breaks on the target hardware.

Android 17's memory limiter hard-kills apps on an undocumented, device-scaled threshold. The existing clearEntities leak (~600 orphaned geometries per S-rank run) turns from a slow degradation into a crash. There is no published number to design against — the only validation is repeated long play sessions on the cheapest supported device.

No webglcontextrestored handler exists. Android WebViews drop the GL context on backgrounding routinely, and the more GPU memory the city keeps resident the more often it will happen. Today that means a permanently frozen game after an incoming call.

Procedural-everything keeps the APK tiny but moves all generation cost to runtime. Without a Web Worker or a strict per-frame build cap, walking across chunk boundaries produces hitches that no amount of draw-call work will fix — and hitches are what the p95 term in quality.js will (correctly) punish by dropping visual quality.

Capacitor WebView has documented reports of running the same content slower than Chrome or a PWA on the same Android device. Validate the WebView delta early with a trivial benchmark scene; if it is large, the entire budget shifts down and some of these targets need renegotiating.

Five to six large distinct biomes plus an open city is an asset-authoring problem at least as large as the engineering problem. The current art is 100% procedural code; scaling that to a believable city means either a lot more procedural code or the first real asset pipeline (glTF + Draco + KTX2), which brings its own memory and load-time budget.

The frustum/visibility scheme depends on chunk Groups being the only thing under the scene root. Any code that adds meshes directly to this.scene (currently _buildPlayer, _spawnEnemy, _spawnBoss, _spawnShadow, Effects.ring all do scene.add directly) bypasses chunk culling entirely and will silently erode the traversal savings.
